scoring_policy: One award for each distinct predeclared anatomical/genetic star-number set or distinct documented stellate morphology / star-named anatomical class. Nested sets may each unlock a different S-index; overlaps must be disclosed. One physical structure does not gain another star merely by receiving multiple equations, transforms or names. Star-number animation rearranges counted units; does not assert physical star geometry.

supporting: Thorax: 12 vertebrae +24 ribs +1 sternum=37; 24 rib bones versus 24 separate presacral vertebrae.
Selected axial 73=22 skull+26 spinal+25 rib cage=80−7 (ossicles 6+hyoid 1).
Anatomical nested shells: 1,13,37,73 with new added units 12,24,36; 73=2×37−1.
Two 37-member sets intersect at 1 sternum: 37+37−1=73; the second set is researcher-defined, not another anatomical region.
24×37=888 appears twice when 24 represents ribs or presacral vertebrae; same 37 parent, not two independent star values.
Anatomical box 8 cranial, 20 metacarpal/metatarsal rays, 26 adult spinal bones; products 160+208+520=888; volume 4160.
Both hands 54 bones; both feet 52; appendicular residual 20; 54+52+20=126.
Reduced name 16+7+10=33 can be instantiated using wrist carpals, one foot tarsals, bilateral metacarpals; 33 spinal segments before fusion.
English simple name 43+38+55=136 matched by 80−37, 10 metacarpals+28 hand phalanges, and 80−25; 55−43=12 thoracic vertebrae.
Anatomical 3|7|7|3 motifs of foot cuneiforms/tarsals and rib regions are positional motifs, not new star numbers.
Genetic 64=61 sense codons +3 stop codons; phi(160)=64 is a separate arithmetic mapping.
Proteasome: 26S complex, 20S core, 4×7=28 core subunits (S are sedimentation labels, not numerals of copies).
Molecular matches reported: histone H3.1 136 residues, mature alpha-globin 141 residues, TGFA 160/HBEGF 208/MMP28 520 residues; protein lengths depend on canonical isoform definitions.
mtDNA 28 heavy-strand genes+9 light-strand genes=37, and 24 RNA+13 protein=37 are distinct partitions of the same 37 genes, not separate stars.
